final.memo:
We have reviewed the ongoing volatility in GameStop and AMC Entertainment and have determined these situations are a pass for our portfolio [D13]. These companies are currently the subjects of intense, retail-driven technical short squeezes that have entirely decoupled share prices from any discernible fundamental value [D13, D208].

When we evaluate investments, we look for a clear margin gap versus peers and a path to earnings growth [D06, D133]. GameStop, with its negative operating margins of -6.2%, stands in stark contrast to the 19.8% operating margins of peers like Best Buy [D06, D133]. Similarly, AMC’s operating margin of 2.5% is significantly inferior to the 10.3% achieved by Cinemark, all while saddled with $4.753bn of debt [D06, D49, D182].

Market participants have seemingly abandoned traditional valuation metrics in favor of sentiment-driven technical feedback loops [D13]. While liquidity is currently high due to the volume of trading, this environment lacks the durable catalysts we require to allocate capital [D13, D114].

Our investment process relies on identifying structural mispricings where we have an edge [D13]. We find no such edge here, as the current price action is disconnected from the secular headwinds facing physical retail and the cinema industry [D159]. We will continue to avoid these speculative situations, as they lack both a fundamental floor and the asymmetric skew required by our mandate [D13].
